messages.author: ee0e84d1caa2a077
messages.subject: inla.hpdmarginal confusing
parts:
Hi
I am confused by the inla.hpdmarginal parametrization:
inla.hpdmarginal(p, marginal, len = 2048L)
When using it, I suspected to get a 95% highest posterior density interval with 
inla.hpdmarginal(.95, marginal, len = 2048L)
However, when I double checked the 95% credible interval from summary.fixed is rather in line with 
inla.hpdmarginal(.975, marginal, len = 2048L).
While I would expect a 95% credible interval from inla.qmarginal(0.975, marginal, len = 2048L) and inla.qmarginal(0.025, marginal, len = 2048L), I wrongly expected a 95% credible interval from inla.hpdmarginal(.95, marginal, len = 2048L).

Is my confusion real or is the confusion just on my side? If it is real, I would suggest hpdmarginal to be reparametrized or to at least make it clear in the documentation of ?inla.hpdmarginal that this p is not the same as in inla.qmarginal.

Best, Dan

P.S. Also it would be helpful for the user if inla.hpdmarginal was described more thoroughly in the help. What kind of credible interval is computed exactly?

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.hpdmarginal confusing
parts:
it is kind of explained here
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credible_interval

but search also for 'HPD interval'

in short, the interval you get from

Prob(x < LOW) = alpha_low
Prob(x > HIGH) = alpha_high

where 1-(alpha_low + alpha_high) = 95%, say

for unimodal distributions, then the shortest interval, ie the choice of
alpha_low that minimize HIGH-LOW, is the HPD interval.

it is somewhat 'weird', as its not invariant for transformations, so...


here is a check:

> r=inla(y~1, data=data.frame(y=0))
> m=r$marginals.fixed$'(Intercept)'
> v = inla.hpdmarginal(0.95, m)
> v
low high
level:0.95 -0.02825688731 0.0281854505
> str(v)
num [1, 1:2] -0.0283 0.0282
- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
..$ : chr "level:0.95"
..$ : chr [1:2] "low" "high"
> inla.pmarginal(v[1,2], m) - inla.pmarginal(v[1,1], m)
[1] 0.95

>
